newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican disputes over election observer funds grows.
newsitem.headline: Mexican disputes over election observer funds grows.

text.p: A dispute over external funding of election observers in Mexico mushroomed on Sunday as three prominent pro-democracy activists criticised the Foreign Ministry for vetoing the use of available European funds.

Santiago Creel Miranda, Jose Agustin Ortiz Pinchetti and Ricardo Pozas told the daily Reforma the government's decision to restrict the access of external funds for watchdog groups was "incongruent" with the need for transparency in elections.
The three former civic counsellors, high-profile apolitical citizens, said transparency would give credibility to the country's transition toward greater democracy.

Mexico's Foreign Ministry was blocking a programme of financing from the European Union to support a project of the Mexican Academy of Human Rights to pay for foreign observers in elections this year.

European Union nations agreed in November 1996 to award $340,000 to the academy to watch over key elections in July. Several governorships will come up for grabs and control of the national congress was also at stake.
The elections include the first ever vote for mayor of Mexico City. The capital's leader has always been hand-picked by the country's president.

Vote rigging and fraud in Mexican elections is not uncommon. The ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) has held the presidency, most governorships and majority control of Congress for 68 years.
Creel Mirando told Reforma the Foreign Ministry decision was a product of the confusion between the functions of the state, the government and the ruling party.
"If the borders are open in an economic sense and in an informational sense, then there is no reason to close them for politics," Pozas said.

Officials from Mexico's Federal Electoral Institute sent a letter on Friday to Foreign Minister Jose Angel Gurria highlighting their concern over the ministry's no-foreign-funds stance and demanding he explain the motive behind the veto.
